key_insight: Continual-learning adapters work best when specialized in intermediate transformer blocks, and a frozen brain-readout signal can pick those blocks without costly placement search.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical way to cut adapter storage and search overhead in vision-transformer continual learning while preserving near-full performance.
method: Search all contiguous 4-block adapter placements across ViT-B/16 backbones.
Use frozen fMRI encoding-model readouts from 12 visual areas to rank blocks by task-dependent variation.
Commit task-specific capacity once to the most variable blocks, with no labels or backpropagation needed.
evidence_signal: Across three ViT-B/16 backbones, LS-B found stable backbone-specific allocations; on Split ImageNet-R it used 60% of full-BiLoRA storage and stayed within 1.5 pp of final accuracy.
watch_item: The chosen blocks are backbone-specific, so the allocation may need recalibration when the backbone or task distribution changes.
paper_title: Two Routes to the Middle: Placement Search and Brain Readouts Converge on Where Continual Learners Should Specialize
